import html # Predefined HTML template with placeholders for the invitation fields. INVITATION_FORMAT = """ {event_name} Invitation
{event_name}
Date: {date_of_event}
{description_of_event}
{notes_block}
""" def create_invitation_for_event( event_name: str, description_of_event: str, date_of_event: str, notes_for_event: str ) -> str: """ Generate a secure, sanitized HTML invitation for an event. Parameters ---------- event_name : str The name or title of the event. description_of_event : str A comprehensive description of the event (may contain newlines). date_of_event : str The scheduled date for the event. notes_for_event : str Extra information or instructions provided by the user. Returns ------- str A string containing sanitized HTML ready for safe rendering. """ # Escape all user-provided content to neutralize any HTML or script injection attempts. escaped_event_name = html.escape(event_name, quote=True) escaped_description = html.escape(description_of_event, quote=True) escaped_date = html.escape(date_of_event, quote=True) escaped_notes = html.escape(notes_for_event, quote=True) # Conditionally include the notes block only if notes are provided. notes_block = "" if escaped_notes.strip(): notes_block = f'
Notes: {escaped_notes}
' # Format the final HTML using the sanitized values. invitation_html = INVITATION_FORMAT.format( event_name=escaped_event_name, date_of_event=escaped_date, description_of_event=escaped_description, notes_block=notes_block ) return invitation_html
